item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WARNING - WINTER STORM - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Severe Winter Weather Warning | Yellow Warning - Winter Storm - In Effect |

Hazardous winter conditions are expected due to: - Snow - Freezing rain - Wind - Rain A significant fall storm will impact northern Manitoba beginning later this evening and will persist through the weekend. Where: Areas of northern Manitoba, including, Pukatawagan, Lynn Lake, Brochet, and Tadoule Lake. What: Hazardous winter conditions including: Heavy snow with total amounts of 20 to 40 cm. Severe wind gusts exceeding 90 km/h. Significantly reduced visibilities in blowing snow. Freezing rain with total amounts of 5 to 10 mm. Heavy rain with total amounts of 20 to 30 mm. When: Precipitation and strong northerly winds will move into northern Manitoba overnight Friday into Saturday morning and begin mostly as rain or freezing rain. This will transition to snow throughout the day on Saturday before tapering off Sunday afternoon. Winds will strengthen throughout the day on Saturday with gusts up to 90 km/h in areas closer to the Nunavut border and will taper off Sunday afternoon and evening. Visibilities will be drastically reduced in blowing snow Saturday afternoon and evening when falling snow and strong winds combine. Travel will likely be hazardous. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced to near-zero at times. Property damage is possible. Property or tree damage is possible. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to MBstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using MBStorm.

| Moderate - possible threat | Expected - act within an hour

item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WARNING - WIND - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Windstorm Warning | Yellow Warning - Wind - In Effect |

Strong damaging winds are expected Saturday through Sunday. Where: Churchill and Arviat What: Strong northeasterly winds on Saturday gusting 100 km/h and strong northwesterly winds on Sunday with gusts possibly exceeding 110 km/h. Reduced visibilities in blowing snow. Remarks: A powerful storm system will move slowly through northern Manitoba and southern Hudson Bay this weekend bringing rain, snow, freezing rain, strong winds and blowing snow. Conditions will slowly improve on Sunday afternoon. Local utility outages are possible. Disruptions to services and travel are possible. Some property damage is possible. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to MBstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using MBStorm.

| Moderate - possible threat | Future - act in near future

item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WARNING - WINTER STORM - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Severe Winter Weather Warning | Yellow Warning - Winter Storm - In Effect |

A significant fall storm will impact northeastern Manitoba and the southern Kivalliq beginning Saturday and will persist through the weekend. Where: Churchill and Arviat What: Hazardous winter conditions including: Snow with total amounts of 10 to 25 cm. Severe wind gusts possibly exceeding 110 km/h. Significantly reduced visibilities in blowing snow. Rain with total amounts of 20 to 30 mm. When: Beginning Saturday morning and tapering off Sunday afternoon. Remarks: Precipitation will move into this area on Saturday as rain or wet snow as wind off the bay will keep temperatures at or above zero. At this time wind speeds will increase with gusts up to 100 km/h. Conditions will transition to snow and blowing snow in the evening and overnight with wind gusts possibly exceeding 110 km/h and drastically reduced visibilities. Snow and winds will gradually taper off Sunday afternoon. Travel will likely be hazardous. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced to near-zero at times. Local utility outages are likely. Property damage is possible. High-sided vehicles will be pushed around by the wind. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to MBstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using MBStorm.

item.title: ACORN Annual Conference & Trade Show
item.description:
ACORN Annual Conference & Trade Show slmacneil Fri, 10/23/2026 - 15:16

Groundwork: From Soil to Sustenance

From building healthy soils and managing pests and disease to exploring new crops, production methods, and ways to make a farm more resilient, Groundwork brings together the knowledge and lived experience that help farms thrive.

Join ACORN for two days of practical learning, conversation, and connection with fellow farmers and growers from across Atlantic Canada.

Whether you’re a seasoned farmer, just getting started, exploring more ecological ways to grow, or simply curious about where our food comes from, you're welcome at the table.

item.title: Province celebrates and invests in community organizations
item.description:
Province celebrates and invests in community organizations jenniferdhogan Fri, 10/23/2026 - 14:59

Today, Minister for Fisheries, Rural Development and Tourism Ernie Hudson wrapped up a week of community celebrations in which he recognized community organizations, commended volunteers, and highlighted investments made through the Rural Growth Initiative (RGI).

"Strong communities are built by people who step up, volunteer, and work together to make life better for their neighbours. Through the Rural Growth Initiative, we are helping local organizations strengthen the places where Islanders gather, learn, stay active, and support one another. These investments are making a real difference in communities across Prince Edward Island, helping them remain vibrant, resilient, and strong for generations to come." 

- Premier Rob Lantz. 

This fiscal year, $6.8 million has been invested in 85 projects around the province, including BGC Montague, supporting the creation of a youth centre that will provide youth programming, leadership development, recreation, and food security supports; the facility upgrades to the West Prince Curling Club, enabling them to host national and regional championships which attract visitors and generate economic activity; and the New Glasgow Rural Community Fire Company Purchasing new bunker gear and portable radios to improve firefighter safety and emergency response capacity.

"The strength of rural Prince Edward Island has always come from the people. Through the Rural Growth Initiative, we are supporting local organizations that provide gathering spaces, recreational opportunities, tourism experiences, emergency services, and community programs that improve the quality of life for those rural Islanders," said Minister of Fisheries, Rural Development and Tourism Ernie Hudson. "These projects reflect the dedication of volunteers and community leaders who continue to invest their time and energy into creating vibrant, inclusive and resilient communities."

RGI supports municipalities and non-profit organizations in delivering community infrastructure and capacity-building projects, including upgrades to community spaces, fire halls, and initiatives that strengthen local services and amenities across rural Prince Edward Island. Since 2019, the Government of Prince Edward Island has invested more than $45.6 million on 878 projects across the three counties through RGI.

More information about the Rural Growth Initiative can be found on the provincial website.

item.title: Statement from Minister Zack Bell on Acadian and francophone community tour
item.description:
Statement from Minister Zack Bell on Acadian and francophone community tour jenniferdhogan Fri, 10/23/2026 - 14:41

Minister responsible for Acadian and Francophone Affairs Zack Bell, issued the following statement at the conclusion of his community tour with Acadians, Francophones, and Francophiles:

“One of the most important first things for me to do in my role as the Minister responsible for Acadian and Francophone Affairs was to get out to the Island’s six Acadian and francophone regions and to hear directly from the people who choose to live in French, and that’s precisely what I did the last few months.

It was a great opportunity to immerse myself in the community, to meet with Acadians, Francophones and Francophiles, and to hear directly from them about what matters most to them and what is needed to ensure that the Acadian and francophone community, as well as the French language can continue to thrive across PEI.

The top concerns raised by participants focused on access to French-language healthcare and government services; the importance of early childhood and K-12 education to support the vitality of the community; the key role community organizations, in particular school-community centres, play in the Acadian and Francophone community; the importance of  Francophone immigration and a sustainable bilingual workforce to support the community’s development; and the importance of the French language and the community’s visibility in Island life.  

Of the numerous conversations I’ve had over the past few months, community members have consistently raised priorities that would be familiar to many Islanders: access to healthcare, education, and a sustainable workforce. 

What made the conversations particularly distinct was the clear message of how important it is to be able to access these services in French while living in a language minority situation. They stressed how valuable it is for their day-to-day and overall vitality of the community to be able to live, work, and participate fully and meaningfully in the language of their choice, no matter where they live on the Island. These conversations were also incredibly informative as they reinforced the priorities that have been consistently identified by the Acadian and Francophone Community Advisory Committee, including their most recent report on the priorities of the community.

I want to thank everyone who came out and took time to share their vision of a vibrant, dynamic Acadian and Francophone community in PEI. The level of engagement, vision, and commitment to a future where anyone who wants to live in French can do so on the Island was evident. 

The work ahead for government is to continue our support for the Acadian and Francophone community, and to help my colleagues ensure that the priority needs of the community are taken into consideration in their work.

Thanks to this tour, I am now better equipped to help my government support the Acadian and Francophone community and to help my colleagues ensure that the needs and priorities of the community are taken into consideration in their work to make sure every Islander can thrive on PEI.”

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
